topic: A clearance application that needed three follow-ups, two visits, and four WhatsApp messages — for one client
format: Walk through the exact day-in-the-life of a Sanad office manager handling 20+ client companies with no case tracking system — every painful step in sequence
post:
11 days until expiry. You found out when the client called.

That's what it took to close one clearance application for one client last week.

While that was happening, 19 other companies were sitting on their own requests — work permits, visa renewals, MOL filings — all of it buried somewhere in a WhatsApp thread you'll have to scroll through for ten minutes to find.

This is what the day actually looks like.

Morning: Client 7 sends a screenshot asking about a permit submitted three weeks ago. You dig through three separate chats just to find the reference number.

Midday: Client 12 calls. Their employee's residency expires in 11 days. You had no idea.

Evening: you're reconciling invoices by hand because nothing in your setup connects a service to a payment.

You're not failing. You're doing solid work inside a system that was never built to hold this much volume.
